evidence_dispersion.rationale: The contract spans two React surfaces, their distinct preparation hooks, and the transport/scheduler boundary across two dependency hops.

contract_opacity.rationale: The foreground generation, invalidation boundary, retry ownership, and invalidateOnClose policy are explicitly named in candidate-visible code.

temporal_composition.rationale: Correctness composes repeated polling, cancellation, stale-generation invalidation, exactly-once delivery, and scope preservation.

schedule_complexity.rationale: Four schedules vary repeated pending states, close timing, response status, and reopen generation.

consumer_heterogeneity.rationale: The foreground dialog owns its work while the background panel merely observes an already-polling workspace-owned job.

repair_locus_ambiguity.rationale: Polling can still be adapted from the background hook or completed in the foreground hook, but the visible generation coordinator identifies the intended lifecycle boundary.

framework_execution_complexity.rationale: The oracle mounts real React components and controls Promise completions, retry callbacks, close, reopen, and unmount boundaries.

structured_judgment.rationale: Structured events still require combining pending, close, generation, and ownership relations.

contract_recovery.rationale: Recovery still compares two consumer policies, but the foreground generation and invalidation operations are explicit.

maintenance.rationale: The patch must complete polling inside an existing lifecycle coordinator without applying foreground ownership to the background consumer.
